A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and complete enough for comparison, including figures, equations and appendices. Despite the changed title and expanded scope, the retained SMC framework, first-order proposal and toy experiments clearly establish continuity.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gaussian-mixture and binarised-MNIST experiments, including reward, EMD, diversity, ESS traces and generated samples in Section 4 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 reports original synthetic, language, DNA and image-generation experiments in Section 4 and Appendix D. Table 5 explicitly attributes some baseline scores to prior work, but the proposed methods have original results.

M1.justification: v3 retains the first-order/Gumbel-Softmax proposal but adds an amortised proposal trained with a log-variance-based objective and an auxiliary mean network. It also introduces product-target/CFG weighting and a shared-position adaptation for low-confidence sampling (Section 3 and Appendix C.2). Appendix D.1 explicitly changes intermediate reward estimation from averaging rewards to log-mean-exp.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates Gaussian mixtures and binarised MNIST. v3 retains these task families and adds prompted toxic-text generation, regulatory DNA design, class-conditional ImageNet256 generation, and text-to-image generation using HPDv2, DrawBench and animal prompts (Sections 4.2–4.4). Figure 1 also introduces a product-target toy scenario.

E2.justification: The corresponding MoG comparison drops v2's brute-force locally optimal oracle and adds learned-proposal variants; the base and gradient variants largely retain their identities under shorter names. v3 introduces BoN comparisons and DNA comparisons against CG, CFG, DRAKES and DRAKES without KL (Table 5). Those DNA baseline scores are attributed to Wang et al., rather than established as new reruns.

E3.justification: Reported reward-estimation sample counts change from 100 to 10 for MoG and from 1 to 10 for MNIST (v2 Section 4; v3 Table 3). Added protocols include 100-token text generation over 15 prompts with 20 generations each, and ImageNet FID/IS evaluation using 50,000 images with particle-count, denoising-step and CFG sweeps. These are changes to retained settings and newly introduced evaluation designs, respectively.

E4.justification: v3 adds temperature-schedule sweeps with an independent MNIST validation classifier and worst-run examples, reward-estimator sample-count sensitivity, proposal-training convergence curves, and particle/step/CFG analyses (Figures 7–11 and Tables 2, 6–10). ReMDM robustness receives more systematic testing. v2's MoG reward/ESS/resampling traces and UDLM experiment are no longer included.

E5.justification: v2 reports sample-set outcomes and trajectories without repeated-run uncertainty estimates. v3 reports means and standard deviations from 30 independent SMC runs per MNIST schedule (Appendix D.2.1), and means with standard deviations across three random seeds for DNA design (Table 5). This introduces substantial replication and uncertainty reporting; it does not establish increased repetition of the original v2 experiments.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive language, DNA and image results and replaces retained toy outcomes. For example, first-order SMC MoG EMD changes from 1.72 in v2 Figure 1 to 2.36 in v3 Figure 2 under changed reward-estimation settings, so this is not a same-setting performance comparison. New Table 2 reports ImageNet FID 14.56 with 16 particles, eight steps and CFG 1.25. v3 Tables 1 and 4 disagree on eight-particle SMCamot perplexity, reporting 147.6 and 127.0 respectively.

T1.justification: v3 adds product-target importance-weight derivations, formal proofs for the existing locally optimal proposal, a uniqueness argument using chi-squared divergence, and a log-variance upper-bound proposition with its proof (Appendix A). Much of v2's continuous-time derivation survives in Appendix B and should not be counted as wholly new. Conversely, v2 Appendix D's carry-over gradient and finite-difference analysis is omitted.

C1.justification: v2 presents a training-free reward-alignment method centred on the first-order proposal and small synthetic/image demonstrations. v3 reframes the contribution as general inference-time scaling through tractable weighting and proposal design, encompassing product targets/CFG, a learned proposal, and applicability across language, biology and text-to-image generation. This substantially expands the claimed contribution beyond rewording.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive discussion of product-target approximation error, learned-proposal reward/diversity tradeoffs, and diminishing or adverse returns from additional particles at stronger CFG settings (Sections 3.1, 4 and Appendix D.2.4). The irreversible-unmasking explanation is retained and supported more systematically. v2's explicit discussion of untested complex applications and future adaptive tempering is removed.

D1.justification: v3 Appendix D.1 adds extensive training recipes: optimisers, learning rates, batch sizes, training budgets, GPU configurations, reward scaling, regularisation, LoRA and pretrained-model sources. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond v2's toy architectures and sampling settings. However, v2's promised project-code link, explicit ESS/partial-resampling settings and detailed carry-over gradient construction are omitted.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around large discrete models, amortised inference, log-variance training and inference-time scaling. Newly cited works include Richter et al. (2020), Richter and Berner (2023), and Dang et al. (2025). Section 5 identifies fixed-proposal SMC approaches as a central contrast, whereas v2 Appendix E emphasised guidance methods and its distinction from Lee et al.

P1.justification: The title, introduction, background, method narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten, with contribution bullets and systematic base/grad/amot terminology. Related work moves from Appendix E into main Section 5, and the appendices are reorganised around proofs, sampling implementation and experimental details. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the addition of experiments.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes predominantly single-column. Toy comparison figures are rebuilt with additional panels, and training/sampling pseudocode appears in paired boxes. v3 adds numerical comparison tables, multi-panel scaling and sensitivity plots, training curves and extensive sample galleries, while removing v2's ESS figure. These are substantial display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v2 Appendix G's central deficiency: effectiveness beyond small datasets and against broader comparators was untested. Multi-domain evaluations, controlled sensitivity studies, independent validation, uncertainty reporting and detailed training recipes now provide substantially stronger support for practical applicability and the learned proposal. The gains outweigh the loss of the carry-over gradient derivation and reporting defects, including conflicting toxicity entries in Tables 1 and 4, although those defects limit confidence in particular results.
